title: Receive and register bulk wool and mohair bulk fibre

lessons.title: Receiving fibre at the store
lessons.html:
The first step in the store

Wool and mohair arrive at the broker's store from farms by truck. Receiving is the first step in the store, and it must be correct. If a bale is wrongly registered, the mistake follows it through weighing, sampling, testing and sale, and the farmer may be paid wrongly.

Before the truck arrives

  • The office may already have the farmer's specification (spec): a list of the bales, their marks, numbers and descriptions.
  • Prepare a clean, dry receiving area.
  • Have the receiving book or computer ready.

When the truck arrives

  1. Get the delivery note from the driver.
  2. Check the truck: was the load covered? Is anything wet or damaged?
  3. Offload safely with the forklift or clamp. Only licensed drivers may do this.
  4. Count the bales or bags and compare with the delivery note and the spec.

Check each bale

  • Farmer's brand or mark clear and correct.
  • Bale number and class description.
  • Pack in good condition, closed, not torn.
  • Dry — wet bales must be reported and kept apart.
  • No signs of contamination like plastic sticking out.

Be polite and clear

The driver also wants to finish quickly. Explain what you are checking and why. If there is a problem, like a wet or torn bale, show the driver, write it on the delivery note, and ask the driver to sign next to your note. This protects the store, the farmer and the driver.

lessons.title: Registering the fibre
lessons.html:
Giving each bale its identity

Registering means recording each bale or lot in the store's system, so it can be traced from arrival to sale.

What to register

ItemExample
Date received2026-03-15
Farmer's name and markJ Mokoena, brand "JM"
Bale numbers1 to 12
Description or classAs marked by the classer
Transporter and delivery note numberFrom the driver's papers
ConditionGood, wet, torn, etc.

The store may give each consignment a reference number or barcode labels. Stick labels where the procedure says, so they can be read later.

Small lots and bags

Small farmers may bring fibre in bags rather than bales. Each bag must still be recorded with the farmer's name and mass, so the farmer is paid correctly when it is binned with other fibre of the same type.

Differences

If the number of bales does not match the delivery note or spec, or marks are missing, write it on the delivery note before signing, and tell the supervisor. Do not "fix" numbers yourself.

Signing

Sign the driver's delivery note only after counting. Give the driver a copy and keep one for the store.

Check twice

Before you finish registering a consignment, read through all the entries again and compare them with the bales in front of you. Look especially at the farmer's mark and the bale numbers. A short check now saves a long search later.

lessons.title: After receiving
lessons.html:
Moving fibre to the next step

  • Move registered bales to the weighing area or to their bay in the store.
  • Keep each farmer's consignment together.
  • Write the bay or location on the record, so bales can be found.
  • Wet bales go to a separate area to dry, as the supervisor says.

Telling the farmer

The office tells the farmer that the clip has arrived and reports any problems, such as wet or damaged bales. This is why your notes must be clear.

Safety during receiving

  • Wear safety boots and a reflective vest.
  • Stay clear of the forklift and never stand under raised loads.
  • Check the truck is parked, the engine is off and wheels are chocked before offloading.
  • Do not climb on the truck load.

Good records

  • Write clearly and check numbers twice.
  • Never rub out a record. Draw one line through a mistake and write the correct value, with your initials.
  • Enter records into the computer on the same day.

Key points

  • Receiving is the first step; mistakes here follow the bale to sale.
  • Count and check every bale against the delivery note and specification.
  • Check marks, numbers, pack condition and dryness; keep wet bales apart.
  • Register each bale with date, farmer, mark, number, description and condition.
  • Note differences on the delivery note before signing and tell the supervisor.

quiz.question: Bales on the truck are fewer than on the delivery note. What do you do?

options.text: Write the difference on the note before signing and tell the supervisor
Change the number on the note to match

quiz.question: What should be done with wet bales?

options.text: Report them and keep them apart
Cover them with plastic and say nothing

quiz.question: Why must each bag from a small farmer be recorded with name and mass?

options.text: So the farmer is paid correctly when it is binned with other fibre
To make the store look busy

quiz.question: When should you sign the driver's delivery note?

options.text: Only after counting and checking the bales
